title: Plex Media Server
comment: Plex keeps everything under one application-support directory ('Plex Media Server': Preferences.xml with the server identity and claim, Library databases, metadata). The FreeBSD package creates it under plexmediaserver_support_path (default /usr/local/plexdata) -- the FreeCORE plugin index ships exactly this jail -- and the Daemonless image exports PLEX_MEDIA_SERVER_APPLICATION_SUPPORT_DIR=/config/Library/Application Support, the same layout the LinuxServer and official pms-docker images keep under /config. Both sources' data paths point at the 'Plex Media Server' directory itself so one carry serves both. rc_data_var is deliberately absent: plexmediaserver_support_path names the PARENT of the data directory, and the override would replace the path wholesale; a jail with a relocated support path is refused with 'required state missing' rather than carrying the wrong tree. The plexpass package variant (rc.d/plexmediaserver_plexpass) is not detected and falls back to the as-is lift. The transcode directory is never carried (the image has its own /transcode volume); media libraries are install-time volumes, not state. Proven 2026-09-29 on a FreeCORE-15.1-RC5 (222345a88d) appliance carrying the #480 catalog fix and this recipe as overlays (both landed on 15.1-stable the same day): a 14.4-RELEASE jail running plexmediaserver 1.43.3.10896 converted in one apply after a per-entry catalog refresh; the server identity carried -- the live /identity endpoint reported the jail's exact ProcessedMachineIdentifier -- on the published 32400 mapping. The source jail was not modified. A Linux bundle mounts /config; the data directory is found inside that mount (the internal development record). hotio/plex is deliberately NOT listed: its data directory is the volume root (/config/Preferences.xml) and it writes TranscoderTempDirectory=/config/Temp into Preferences.xml, which needs a remap and a preference rewrite (per-image layouts, the internal development record).
drop: transcode directory (the image has its own /transcode volume)
